title: Session-affinity Ingress Orchestrator Terraform Module (internal NLB->ALB, TLS options)
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a reusable Terraform module that implements an internal ingress orchestration pattern: NLB in front for TCP passthrough and cross-AZ stable IPs, ALB for HTTP/HTTPS routing and TLS termination, optional mTLS, session-affinity (cookie/IP-based) for stateful backends, connection-draining and health checks tuned for long-lived KV-cache sessions. Module must support zero-downtime cert rotation, ABI-compatible inputs with existing internal-ingress modules, and work in Private (VPC) deployments with strict network egress controls.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module published to our internal registry with a stable version >= 1.0.0
Module exposes variables for: nlb_enabled, alb_enabled, tls_mode (off|pass-through|termination|mtls), session_affinity (none|cookie|source_ip), cert_arn, cert_rotation_policy
Integration tests pass in a staging VPC with cross-AZ traffic and simulated KV cache workload showing <5% additional tail latency compared to baseline
Can perform cert rotation with zero 5xxs and connection draining respecting client keepalive windows
Documentation and example usage (simple app + canary) in Confluence and sample-terraform repo
Security review completed and KMS/HSM patterns documented
design_notes: Decisions: prefer NLB first hop for predictable client IP & static AZ IPs. Use ALB for path-based routing and TLS termination where features (redirects, host-based routing) are required. Support two execution paths: TCP passthrough via NLB -> target group (for model servers expecting mutual TLS) and HTTP termination at ALB with ALB-target groups. Session-affinity will default to cookie for HTTP and stickiness for TCP via source IP. We'll implement cookie-based sticky session by creating an ALB target group with 'stickiness' enabled and configuring the cookie name via variable. For NLB IP stickiness, rely on target group source_ip type plus connection_draining. Healthchecks: support configurable healthy/unhealthy thresholds and interval tuned for model warming (longer initial timeout). Certificate rotation: support a 'staged' mode where new cert is applied to ALB listeners with lower priority, then promote after validation.
terraform_interface: variables: {vpc_id, private_subnets, nlb_enabled, alb_enabled, tls_mode, cert_arn_primary, cert_arn_staging, session_affinity, target_groups=[{name, port, protocol, healthcheck}], idle_timeout, connection_draining_seconds, cross_zone_load_balancing, tags}; outputs: {nlb_dns, alb_dns, listener_arns, target_group_arns, module_version}
migration_strategy: Provide a compatibility wrapper that accepts legacy variables from ENG-77456-style modules. For existing stacks: add canary ALB with new module in same VPC, route a 5% sample traffic using weighted internal DNS (Route53 private) or traffic mirroring. After 48h of metrics validation (latency, 5xx rate, connection counts), flip 100% and decommission legacy resources. Provide terraform plan snippets and an automated migration script in tools/infra-scripts.
test_plan: Unit: terraform validate + fmt + static analysis via tflint and checkov
Integration: deploy to staging VPC with 3 AZs, simulate 2000 rps with long-lived streaming requests; assert session affinity preserves client-target mapping across retries
Chaos test: kill a target behind ALB/NLB during heavy KV-cache workload to verify connection draining and failover behavior
Cert rotation test: rotate staging->primary cert and verify no 5xx spikes and no TLS handshake failures
Security scan: check KMS usage, least-privilege IAM roles for ELB actions
rollout_plan: Merge PR with module and tag v1.0.0-rc
Deploy module to staging with sample-app using session_affinity=cookie
Run integration and chaos tests (48h window) and review dashboards
Run security review and get signoff from security team
Create canary in customer-like staging (private-reserved-capacity) at 5% traffic
Promote to 100% and cut release branch private-2025.03
Post-rollout: monitor for 72h and collect metrics into console: per-listener latency, 5xx, connection_count, target_health

Design (Rina Gupta): requested an example showing mTLS handshake config and KMS key rotation guidance
